court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Jaiprakash Madhukarrao Sahurkar vs Sarika W/O Jaiprakash Sahurkar
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: The applicant and non-applicant were married in 1999. Differences arose in 2013, leading to a complaint filed by the non-applicant against the applicant under Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code. The parties arrived at an amicable settlement in 2014, but the applicant later filed for divorce.

legal_principles.principle: The applicant cannot be compelled to undergo the rigour of trial under Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005 on the basis of same allegations.
legal_principles.held: Once it is found by the Court of competent jurisdiction that the non-applicant has failed to establish that the applicant had subjected the non-applicant to cruelty contemplated by Section 498-A of the Indian Penal Code, the applicant cannot be put to double jeopardy of undergoing the trial under the provisions of Section 12 of the Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
cited_cases: Markapuram Siva Rao s/o Somaiah vs. State of Andhra Pradesh and another in Criminal Petition No.12970 of 2010
G.G.A. Naidu vs. State of Maharashtra & Ors. reported in 2002 ALL MR (Cri.) 1465
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent harassment and abuse of process

legal_principles.principle: The findings recorded by the learned Magistrate while acquitting the applicant of the charge under Section 498-A and Section 323 of the Indian Penal Code are binding on the non-applicant.
legal_principles.held: It is submitted that the maxim 'res-judicata provertitate accipitur' is applicable to the criminal proceedings also.
cited_cases: Pritam Singh and another vs. The State of Punjab reported in AIR 1956 SC 415
legal_principles.significance: HIGH — to prevent harassment and abuse of process

outcome.final_order: The order passed by the learned Magistrate was set aside and the proceedings initiated by the non-applicant under Section 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 were quashed.
